text.p: American 200 metres champion Jon Drummond professed himself baffled on Wednesday after former world champion Frankie Fredericks set the fastest qualifying time of 20.13 seconds in the world quarter-finals.

Drummond, who was almost eliminated in the morning's first round when he lost his balance and narrowly avoided stepping into an adjoining lane, qualified in third place in 20.59 seconds behind Fredericks and Ato Boldon.
"Well, Frankie certainly sent a message to the rest of us with that run," Drummond said. "But I'm not sure what he was trying to prove.
"I saw Frankie and Ato going for it, but I wasn't getting into that. Why waste all that energy at this stage of the game, what was that all about?"

Boldon, who bombed in the 100 final on Sunday after his early round form suggested he would destroy the opposition, clocked 20.28 and said: "Nothing is going to make up for the disappointment of what happened in the 100, but I'm still going out to win this."

In the women's 200, Susanthika Jayasinghe added her own contribution to a significant day of sporting achievement for Sri Lanka, by clocking the second fastest qualifying time in the quarter-finals. One the day that her country's cricketers set

a record test score in a test match, Jayasinghe made people sit up and take notice of her 22.47 second run which guaranteed her a place in the semifinals on Wednesday. Only Melinda Gainsford of Australia with 22.45 ran faster.
Gold medal favourite Marie Jose Perec of France also coasted into the last 16 with a time of 22.69 running into a headwind and said afterwards she was happy with her performance.
"It was much better than the way I ran in the opening round this morning," said the double Olympic champion. "There was a very strong headwind, but it didn't really bother me."
Merlene Ottey, bidding for her third successive world 200 title also came through effortlessly, winning the opening heat in 22.65 seconds.

Ottey, whose hopes in the 100 were effectively dashed when she sprinted 60 metres after failing to hear the recall gun following a false start, said: "This is nothing to get excited about, anything can happen in athletics. There are two more rounds to go yet."
